analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: REVERSAL
key_insights: S&P 500 closed +158bps at 7,688 with a $2bn market-on-close imbalance to sell. NDX +91bps at 28,437, R2K +151bps at 2,854, Dow +303bps at 53,356. Volume was 21.727bn shares vs a year-to-date daily average of 18.509bn.
VIX fell 1954bps to 16.76, WTI crude fell 782bps to $88.57, the US 10-year yield fell 7bps to 4.88%, gold rose 343bps to 4,064, DXY fell 35bps to 101.51 and Bitcoin rose 307bps to $80,198.

The market bid aggressively after the midterms. President Trump told the NYT he would accept the election results, which removed some left-tail risk. Crude fell 8% and Brent returned to about $95, below the $100 level, which renewed an index-level bid across markets.

Consumer was the largest net beneficiary of lower yields and oil, light positioning, and views of less pressure on spending programs such as SNAP in future budget and debt negotiations. Retail rose 5.5%, or +390bps relative to SPY, the 2nd largest 1-day outperformance in the last 2 years.
XRT is at 5-year highs and XLP is at an all-time high.
The GS floor rated activity 6 on a 1-10 scale and finished +2% better to buy. Asset manager and hedge fund net flow skews finished roughly balanced.

The largest theme on the GS desk was net buying of hyperscalers against supply in semis, from a mix of client types. The desk's read is that the new political backdrop favors owners of compute (hyperscalers) and hurts those who build out, sell into or power datacenters (neoclouds, semis, power).
Exchange volumes ran 30%+ above the 20-day average.

After the close, QCOM fell 4% on a revenue guide described as solid with mixed EPS and EBIT. ZG fell 22% on revenue and EBITDA misses. APP rose 15% on a large beat and guidance well above expectations.

John Flood says equity investors across cohorts have had a difficult stretch since July, with significant risk cut. Hedge fund net exposure is historically low and gross ticked lower last week. Long-only funds hold significant cash raised during the July and October selloffs, and most has not been redeployed.

October is the most significant fiscal year-end month for mutual funds by AUM and fund count. Long-only funds sold stocks on 10/30 because of year-end dynamics, which set up the midterms as a clean positioning clearing event.
GS says the most important potential clearing event this year is still ahead and is tied to equity capital markets.

Derivatives desk: post-election focus moved to rotation away from AI infrastructure and a sharp reversion in vol. Event risk premium came out of the surface overnight and the vol crush continued through the day as all 3 indices reversed an initial selloff.

S&P Dec fixed-strike vol fell 1.2 vol points and short-dated calls are again under 11 vol. The market has rallied back into a long gamma area, but topside vols are low enough that the desk thinks a further rally would lift vol.
Over 530k VIX calls traded in the first hour, mostly sold, as the desk saw tail hedges monetized. VVIX fell 18 points at the intraday low and settled down 17.
Flows were concentrated in covering and hedge unwinds with little new length. The desk saw Dec upside restructuring in UAL and DAL.
The desk prefers owning SPX over NDX because vols screen as more attractive. The straddle for the rest of the week traded at 91bps.

GIR on midterms: larger-than-expected majorities could give Democrats slightly more leverage with the White House but dilute small factions within the caucus. GIR expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to try to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse last year's spending cuts.
